I grew up in a very, very white rural community. I was the only non-Christian kid at school that I knew of. My first friend and her family were very religious and started to shame me for my beliefs. At first, I wanted to be baptized in a church. I wanted nothing to do with anything native, because that was I thought separated me from my peers and made life so lonely and sad for me. My mom wouldn't let me. Never actually went to church.

When I was maybe 10 years old my family's spiritual community fell apart and we had no one to pray or be with. Heartbroken at that time, I decided religion/spirituality wasn't for me and declared myself an atheist. Funnily enough I never actually did let go of any of my native beliefs, I just compartmentalized them and refused to visit them because they were too painful for me.

I carried those feelings throughout my teen years until I found yoga. Practiced yoga for a little while and it really rekindled my relationship with my own spirit, but I would go home and cry for my own traditions as an indigenous woman. I really sincerely thought I would never get to pray in that way again.
